acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Gargoyles family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Grotesque, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Perch-Drop Initiate (Initiate) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Small perched chipped-sandstone figure with crude features and wings too small to be useful for flight.
Signature mechanic: Chipped Drop: the perched Grotesque releases both claws for a low body slam, then scrapes back to its pedestal fragment.
battlefieldDuty: Probe approach timing with one short drop from a low architectural perch.
constructionDimensions: Material/structure branches: T1 chipped sandstone, tiny useless wings, perch chip, and crude water-spout mouth gain one crystal mortar key; T2 granite, moss, and small wings gain sediment-set hop joints; T3 broad wings, carved relief, and amber seams gain load ribs; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery gain fracture braces; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants gain bounded throne faults.

Motion/process branches: T1 one short perch drop loads the water-spout mortar key; T2 a hop with small wings commits one granite joint; T3 the dive with broad wings transfers load through relief ribs; T4 a tracery aisle plants through its bronze brace; T5 each attendant command loads and releases one throne fault.
counterplay: Leave the short drop lane and strike the loaded toe or tiny wing root during the scrape back. Affinity signal: Affinity counterplay branches: T1 the chipped-sandstone perch and tiny wings expose the water-spout mortar fault after landing; T2 the granite moss line and small-wing hinge expose a loaded joint after the hop; T3 broad wings and amber relief seams expose a load-rib fracture after the dive; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery expose the committed brace; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants expose the commanded throne fault after its load releases.
identityInvariants: Squat crouched construction, hunched shoulders, horned beast face, clawed grip, and folded architectural wings remain recognizable.
Sandstone, granite, marble, bronze, mortar, moss, and water staining remain discrete built materials rather than flesh.
Relief carving, water-spout mouths, restrained amber seams, and pedestal fragments preserve the architectural source grammar.
Stone quality and wing architecture escalate from useless carved flaps to sovereign buttresses while load-bearing joints stay readable.
telegraph: Crude features tilt down and dust falls from the chipped toe that bears the perch load.
